evals.name: tekmetric-ram-brake-tow-in
evals.prompt: Can you check this inspection my shop sent? My truck got towed in because the brakes went soft. I'm the owner, it's in California. The front calipers were done a few months ago at a different shop.
evals.notes: Real customer report (2001 Dodge Ram 2500, Tekmetric). Kept out of git because it contains personal data; place a copy at the path above to run.
evals.expected_output: Consumer-mode audit that mirrors the shop's item structure, flags the report's self-contradictions, puts the leak repair first, routes the caliper warranty question to the customer, and ends with a ready-to-send message.

assertions.text: Lists a dedicated conflicting-statements section
Flags 'towed in for loss of brakes' vs a test drive reporting brake feel
Flags 'calipers recently replaced' vs 'replace both front calipers'
States that the recommendation does not repair the leaking banjo bolt / fitting the shop identified as the cause
Flags the red Front Brake System grade alongside 'pads 7+mm good condition'
Notes there is no mileage on the report and that schedule-based items cannot be verified
Keeps 'Differential & Transfer Case' as one item (front diff, rear diff, transfer case) with per-part verdicts rather than splitting it
Identifies the rear differential service as overlapping the rear cover reseal
Flags 'all 4 tie rod ends' as wider than the single documented tie rod end with play
Puts the leak repair plus bleed in Fix now and makes the master cylinder conditional on a pedal test
Tells the customer to check caliper warranty with the shop that installed them, and does not ask the current shop who did the work
Notes the printed PDF photos are thumbnails too small to verify
Includes a ready-to-send message to the shop with no accusatory words (scam, ripoff, fraud, upsell)
Does not repeat the customer's name

evals.name: tekmetric-ram-followup-discontinued-parts
evals.prompt: Follow-up on the same Ram inspection: I asked the shop why replacing the calipers and master cylinder fixes a leak. They said the parts were discontinued so they had to get all new parts to fix the leak. Does that make sense?
evals.notes: Second turn after eval 1. Tests the follow-up step: judging a verbal shop explanation.
evals.expected_output: Explains why the answer doesn't fully hold up, asks for a verifiable specific, notes what it leaves unexplained, keeps the work on hold, and points to the installing shop.

assertions.text: Notes that banjo bolts and sealing washers are generally standard, widely available parts, without claiming certainty about this truck
Points out that if new calipers can be bought, the fittings that come with them can be too
Notes the explanation does not justify the master cylinder replacement
Notes the explanation is verbal and absent from the report, and suggests getting it in writing
Asks for the specific discontinued part number and supplier
Recommends holding the calipers and master cylinder while checking with the shop that installed the calipers
Includes a short, non-accusatory reply the customer can send
